title: Length: Measuring and Converting mm, cm, m and km
seo_title: Grade 5 Length Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order 2-D shapes and 3-D objects using measuring instruments such as rulers, metre sticks, tape measures and trundle wheels; use millimetres (mm), centimetres (cm), metres (m) and kilometres (km); calculate and solve problems involving length; convert between mm, cm, m and km.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 length worksheets: choosing units, reading scales, converting mm, cm, m and km and length problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Same unit before adding or subtracting.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 10 mm = 1 cm, 100 cm = 1 m, 1 000 m = 1 km.
  • Choose a sensible unit: mm for an ant, cm for a book, m for a classroom, km for a road.
  • To change to a smaller unit, multiply; to change to a bigger unit, divide.
  • Change to the same unit before you add or subtract.

Examples

Example

3 km − 850 m

3 km = 3 000 m

3 000 − 850

Answer: 2 150 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
100 m in a km1 km = 1 000 m.
Multiplying to a bigger unitmm to cm: divide by 10.
Different unitsChange to the same unit first.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the height of a tall gum tree?
items.e: A tall gum tree is many metres high. Centimetres would give a huge number, and kilometres are far too big.

items.q: Choose the best estimate for the height of a Grade 5 learner.
items.e: Most Grade 5 learners are between 1 m 30 cm and 1 m 50 cm tall, so 140 cm fits. 140 mm is only 14 cm, the size of a hand.

items.q: Pieter measures his book. It is between 24 cm and 25 cm long. Which unit should he use to give a more accurate measure?
items.e: A smaller unit gives a more accurate measure. 1 cm = 10 mm, so he can measure to the nearest millimetre, for example 247 mm.

items.q: Which measure of a pencil is the most accurate?
items.e: Millimetres are the smallest unit here. 164 mm (16 cm 4 mm) is more accurate than 16 cm, which leaves out the extra 4 mm.

The pencil starts at 0. It ends 4 small marks past 7 cm. 7 cm = 70 mm, and 70 + 4 = 74 mm. (80 mm reads the next number, 8, instead of counting the small marks.)
The crayon starts at 2 cm, not 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm. 83 mm − 20 mm = 63 mm = 6 cm 3 mm. (8 cm 3 mm forgets that the crayon does not start at 0.)
The rubber starts at 1 cm (10 mm) and ends at 48 mm. 48 − 10 = 38 mm. (48 mm forgets that it starts at 1 cm. 30 mm counts only the whole centimetres.)
The pencil ends 7 small marks past 9 cm, so it is 9 cm 7 mm (97 mm). 9 cm and 10 cm are only to the nearest centimetre. 97 cm uses the wrong unit.
The crayon ends 8 small marks past 5 cm, so it is 5 cm 8 mm (58 mm). 6 cm is the nearest whole centimetre, but 5 cm 8 mm is more accurate.

items.e: There are 9 small marks between 3 and 4, but 10 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks. Each space is 1 mm, and 10 mm = 1 cm.

items.e: The numbers go up by 10 cm. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 cm ÷ 10 = 1 cm. Count the spaces after 140 cm: 141 cm, 142 cm, 143 cm. So it is 143 cm.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Kilo means 1 000, so 1 kilometre = 1 000 metres. A kilometre is about a 15-minute walk.

items.q: Convert. 3 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1 000: 3 × 1 000 = 3 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3 km = 3 000 m. (300 m multiplies by 100, but 1 km is 1 000 m.)

items.q: Convert. 12 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1 000: 12 × 1 000 = 12 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 12 km = 12 000 m. (1 200 m multiplies by 100 instead of 1 000.)

items.q: Convert. 40 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 40 × 10 = 400. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 40 cm = 400 mm. (4 mm divides when it should multiply.)

items.q: Convert. 20 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1 000: 20 × 1 000 = 20 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 20 km = 20 000 m. (2 000 m uses × 100. Check: 20 km is 20 groups of 1 000 m.)

items.q: 14 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 14 of 100 cm = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm.

items.q: 15 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 15 of 100 cm = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 cm.
